overall_quality.evidence: Processes and threads are both fundamental concepts in computer science, but they serve different purposes and have distinct characteristics. Processes are independent units of execution that can run concurrently, while threads are lightweight sub-processes that share the same memory space and resources. Processes are more resource-intensive and have higher overhead, but they offer better isolation and security. Threads, on the other hand, are more efficient and can share data and resources more easily, but they can also introduce synchronization and deadlock issues.
